children: U.S. jobless claims sank last week, the latest sign of a resilient economy that could force policymakers to hike rates further this year.

The number of people who filed for unemployment benefits was 196,000 in the week through Sept. 12, 10,000 lower than the unrevised 206,000 reported a week earlier, the Labor Department said Thursday. Economists surveyed by The Wall Street Journal were expecting to see the figure tick up to 207,000.

Continuing claims, which scale with the total size of the unemployed population, totaled 1.73 million in the week through Sept. 5, sliding by 39,000 from the downwardly revised total a week earlier. The data on continuing claims lag the initial-claims data by a week.

Persistent signs of a strong labor market will put pressure on the Federal Reserve to continue tightening monetary policy going forward. The central bank raised rates on Wednesday for the first time in three years as it pushes to get inflation under control.
